\label{T: main}
For $n\geq 3$ let $\Gamma_{2n}$ be the graph whose vertices are the $(n-1,n)$-flags of $\PG(2n,q)$, with two vertices being adjacent if the corresponding flags are opposite. For $q$ large enough compared to $n$, a maximal coclique $\mathcal{F$ of $\Gamma_{2n}$ falls into exactly one of the following categories.
\begin{enumerate} [(a)]
    \item $|\mathcal{F|=\Gauss{2n}{n-1} \Gauss{n+1}{1} +\Gauss{2n-1}{n-1}q^n$ and $\mathcal{F$ is one of the structures described in Example \ref{E: main}.
    \item $|\mathcal{F|\leq \Gauss{2n}{n-1} \Gauss{n+1}{1} +f(n,q)\cdot q^n$ and there is either a hyperplane $H$, such that $\mathcal{F$ contains all flags $(A,B)$ with $B\subseteq H$, or there is a point $P$ such that $\mathcal{F$ contains all flags $(A,B)$ with $P\subseteq A$.
    \item $|\mathcal{F|$ is at most $\mathcal{O(q^{n^2+n-2})$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
\begin{proof}
First, assume that the number  of flags in \(\mathcal{F\} that contain \(B\) is \(\Gauss{n+1}{1}\). This means that for every \((n-1)\)-space \(A\) contained in \(B\), we have \((A,B)\in \mathcal{F\}. Let \((A',B')\) be an \((n-1,n)\)-flag of \(\PG(2n,q)\) with \(A'\cap B=\emptyset\). Then \(B\cap B'\) is just a point \(P\). There exist \((n-1)\)-spaces in \(B\) that are skew to \(P\). Therefore, there are flags in \(\mathcal{F\} that are opposite to \((A',B')\), hence \((A',B')\) is not in \(\mathcal{F\}.

    Now, assume that every flag \((A',B')\in \mathcal{F\} satisfies \(A'\cap B\neq \emptyset\). Then every flag \((A,B)\), where \(A\) is an \((n-1)\)-space contained in \(B\), is non-opposite to all flags in \(\mathcal{F\}. By maximality of \(\mathcal{F\}, all such flags are in \(\mathcal{F\}. The number of flags in \(\mathcal{F\} containing \(B\) is \(\Gauss{n+1}{n}=\Gauss{n+1}{1}\).

    Finally, assume that there exist \((n-1,n)\)-flags in \(\mathcal{F\} whose \((n-1)\)-spaces are skew to \(B\). Let \((A'_1,B'_1),\ldots,(A'_k,B'_k)\) be all these flags. Now, any flag \((A,B)\in \mathcal{F\} has to satisfy \(A\cap B'_1\neq\emptyset,\ldots, A\cap B'_k\neq\emptyset\). 
    Let \(1\leq i\leq k\).
    As \(A'_i\cap B=\emptyset\), we know that \(B'_i\cap B\) is a point, say \(P_i\).
    Now \(A\) has to be incident with all points \(P_i\). In other words, the span of the points \(P_i\) has to be incident with \(A\). Let \(s\) be the dimension of the span \(S\) of the points \(P_i\).
    We have \(0\leq s\leq n-1\), otherwise there could be no flag in \(\mathcal{F\} that contains \(B\). 
    By maximality of \(\mathcal{F\}, any \((n-1)\)-space \(A\) that is incident with \(S\) and \(B\) occurs in a flag \((A,B)\) of \(\mathcal{F\}. There are \(\Gauss{n-s}{(n-1)-s}=\Gauss{n-s}{1}\) such flags.
\end{proof}

Proof
nodes.statement:
By \Cref{L: many yellow pw skew}, there are $n+1$ pairwise skew yellow $(n-1)$-spaces, or $n+1$ yellow $n$-spaces in pairwise general position in \PG(2n,q). We assume that \PG(2n,q) contains $n+1$ pairwise skew $(n-1)$-spaces $A_1,\ldots,A_{n+1}$ and show that the number of flags in \mathcal{F$ is \mathcal{O(q^{n^2+n-2})$, for yellow $n$-spaces dual arguments suffice.
     
     Let $1\leq i\leq n+1$. 
     Any flag $(A,B)\in \mathcal{F$ satisfies $B\cap A_i=\emptyset$ or $B\cap A_i\neq\emptyset$.
     By the dual statement of \Cref{L: yellows meet almost all}, the number of flags $(A,B)\in \mathcal{F$ with distinct $(n-1)$-spaces and with $A_i\cap B=\emptyset$ is at most \mathcal{O(q^{n^2-1})$. As the red spaces are already accounted for, we can safely assume that these $(n-1)$-spaces are all yellow. This yields that the number of flags $(A,B)\in \mathcal{F$ with $A_i\cap B=\emptyset$ is \mathcal{O(q^{n^2-1})\Gauss{n}{1}=\mathcal{O(q^{n^2+n-2})$. 
     
     Hence, the number of flags $(A,B)\in \mathcal{F$ with $A_i\cap B=\emptyset$ for some $1\leq i\leq n+1$ is $(n+1)\mathcal{O(q^{n^2+n-2})=\mathcal{O(q^{n^2+n-2})$. All other flags in \mathcal{F$ must have an $n$-space that meets $A_1,\ldots,A_{n+1}$. By \Cref{L: few that meet all}, the number of $n$-spaces that meet $A_1,\ldots,A_{n+1}$ is \mathcal{O(q^{n^2-1})$. As the red spaces are already accounted for, we can safely assume that these $n$-spaces are all yellow. This yields that the number of flags $(A,B)\in \mathcal{F$ with $A_i\cap B\neq\emptyset$ for all $1\leq i\leq n+1$  is also \mathcal{O(q^{n^2-1})\Gauss{n}{1}=\mathcal{O(q^{n^2+n-2})$. 
\end{proof}
